responsiveHiddenAcceptedUnchecked.classifier: isAcceptedUnchecked() = kind === "responsive-hidden" && media !== undefined. responsiveHiddenAcceptedUnchecked.mediaBandProof: hiddenRanges() (layout-inference.ts:661-684) only opens a band over a contiguous run of HIDDEN probe widths, and the emission site is gated on vAt(truthEntry.i) === 1, i.e. the node is VISIBLE at 1440. Band start = floor(midpoint(visible_below, first_hidden)) > 1440 when 1440 is the visible neighbour below; band end = floor(midpoint(last_hidden, visible_above)) - 0.02 < 1440 when 1440 is the visible neighbour above. LAYOUT_PROBE_WIDTHS = [390,768,1024,1440,1920] are far enough apart that no midpoint can land on 1440. Proof intact after the refactor.

referenceDiscoveryReview.falsePositives: HARMLESS BY CONSTRUCTION. A `var(--x)` appearing inside a url() string, an SVG <text> node, a title/desc, or any other attribute text produces an extra name, which is then resolved with getComputedStyle at the consuming element. If it resolves to "" it is dropped and counted; if it resolves, the name is a genuinely declared custom property and emitting it on the wrapper is inert (custom properties only take effect where a var() consumes them). Cost is one extra getPropertyValue call. outerHTML escaping cannot break the match either — `var(--x)` contains no escapable character.
referenceDiscoveryReview.falseNegatives: names containing escapes or non-ASCII characters are missed. Under-report, never a wrong value.
referenceDiscoveryReview.elementResolution: CONFIRMED as described — getComputedStyle(inlineSvgElements[i]) where inlineSvgElements is a parallel array pushed in the same svg branch of the DFS walk (collect-dom.ts:746-747), so index alignment and document order are structural, not incidental. The markup scanned is inlineSvgs[i].outerHTML, i.e. the exact string the pipeline copies verbatim.
referenceDiscoveryReview.sheetWinsPrecedence: CONFIRMED (collect-dom.ts:1102 `if (seenCustomNames[name] === true) continue;` after incrementing referenceSheetKnownCount). Reproduced live on my own fixture: --brand is both SVG-referenced and sheet-discovered, and comes out counted 1 in referenceSheetKnownCount, NOT re-resolved, NOT duplicated, value still the sheet's #112233.
referenceDiscoveryReview.documentOrderConflictRule: CONFIRMED. Reproduced live on my own fixture: --clash-tone declared #010203 on .zone-a and #030201 on .zone-b, each with its own SVG — captured value is #010203 (the first consuming element in document order) and referenceResolutionConflicts = 1.
referenceDiscoveryReview.counterClosure: CONFIRMED on an uncapped run. Sheet channel: discoveredCount = kept + unresolvedCount + valueCapped. Reference channel: referenceDiscoveredCount = referenceSheetKnownCount + referenceResolvedCount + referenceUnresolvedCount. My fixture closed at 4 = 1 + 2 + 1; linear closed at 16 = 0 + 16 + 0. CAVEAT: reference-channel cap drops fold into the SHARED valueCappedCount / countCapped, so per-channel closure only holds when no cap fires (defect C3, informational — the folding is documented as intentional).

defects.finding: The docstring says 'Failure to verify never fails the generation'. Exceptions thrown by browser.newContext(), context.newPage(), context.route() or by the browserPage.close()/context.close() calls in the per-page `finally` sit OUTSIDE both the import/launch guards and the per-page try/catch, so they propagate out of verifyLayoutRules and abort generateApp() (which does not wrap the call — generate-app.ts:248).

defects.finding: The docstring claims ':root { &.x { --a } } and :root { @media … { --b } } BOTH contribute'. isSelfSelector only returns true for a selector part that is exactly '&', so '&.x' does NOT inherit the root context. Measured live on my own fixture: with ':root { &.x { --nested: 9px } @media (min-width: 1px) { --nested2: 8px } }', discoveredCount was 6 and --nested2 was captured while --nested was NOT.
defects.impact: under-report only, never a wrong value (and ':root.x' would usually resolve to nothing on documentElement anyway). No effect on the linear measurement.
defects.fix: either accept a nested part beginning with '&' when inRoot, or correct the docstring example

defects.kind: precedence keyed on discovered rather than kept
defects.finding: Sheet precedence skips element resolution whenever seenCustomNames[name] is true — i.e. whenever the sheet walk DISCOVERED the name, even if that name was subsequently DROPPED (resolved to '' at documentElement and counted in unresolvedCount, or dropped by the value cap, or sliced off by the count cap). A value the consuming element would have resolved is then lost.
defects.impact: zero on linear.app (referenceSheetKnownCount = 0). It is counted (referenceSheetKnownCount) rather than silent, and the direction is under-report.
defects.fix: key precedence on the kept set (names actually pushed into customProperties) instead of seenCustomNames

defects.kind: shared cap counters break per-channel closure
